method: Compare published IVTFF side/panel convention, source locus-type counts, and a bounded Yale image derivative. Source counts and opening source loci were inspected before the image; this is not a blinded or independent concordance test.

naming_reference.scope: Recto panel names progress away from the binding; the diagram illustrates 72, not a source-specific image/text alignment for 67r.

panels.proposed_panel_locator: Left field of the displayed scan, nearest the visible binding, left of the principal vertical crease.
direct_observations: Four horizontal text rows appear above the large circular drawing.
The drawing has colored radial shapes around a central face-like form, writing in circular bands, and writing extending along radial divisions.
panels.placement_hypothesis: The four P0 locations correspond to the four upper horizontal rows, in source order.

panels.proposed_panel_locator: Right field of the displayed scan, farther from the binding, right of the principal vertical crease.
direct_observations: The circular drawing contains a small central star-like form, surrounding crescent-like marks, and writing distributed across compartments and rings.
Three horizontal text rows appear below the drawing; the middle row is red.
panels.placement_hypothesis: The three P0 locations correspond to the three lower horizontal rows, in source order.

review_test: At original resolution, check the source locations against the proposed horizontal rows, preserving spacing and reading alternatives.
Reject or revise a placement if source order, row count, or glyph sequences disagree; do not choose a preferred edition to repair the mismatch.
Record reviewed region boundaries and any crossing text before creating a verified image/text join.
limits: No exact panel mask, pixel bounding box, or crop is assigned.
Agreement of locus-type counts is not agreement of glyph readings or independent replication between editions.
Circular and radial source locations have not been assigned to individual image regions.
No linguistic content, celestial identification, decoding, or translation is inferred.
Both panels remain one leaf and one image dependency; this observation supplies no untouched evaluation material.
